_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); orders, revenue and margin signals; the listing and short-history bounds rules

pit_profile.why: Baker Hughes: 'We are a fullstream provider of oilfield products, services and digital solutions'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may curtail production and demand for hydrocarbons such as oil and natural gas by shifting demand towards and investment in relatively lower carbon energy sources such as wind, solar and other renewables' (its own FY2018 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here

classification.quality_note: Baker Hughes: 'We are a fullstream provider of oilfield products, services and digital solutions'; 'Our revenue is predominately generated from the sale of products and services to major, national, and independent oil and natural gas companies worldwide, and is dependent on spending by our customers for oil and natural gas exploration, field development and production'; 'We operate in a highly competitive environment, which may adversely affect our ability to succeed'; 'may curtail production and demand for hydrocarbons such as oil and natural gas by shifting demand towards and investment in relatively lower carbon energy sources such as wind, solar and other renewables' (its own FY2018 10-K): revenues and earnings that follow customers' spending on exploration, development and production through the commodity cycle, by the company's own account; ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining, which an oilfield services and equipment company does not hold, so the climate-change wording stays here. cyclical (obsolescence risk 2/5); price cheap; Ratio B -0.00x; +11% to EPP floor; model-vs-market gap +1.28; conservative 2yr +64%.

BEAR.desc: Flat EPS (no EPS change in FY18-FY18 to measure: the 0% cap); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.1%/yr (Q1 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 1.4-yr ex-FY17 median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.1%/yr (no FY18-FY18 CAGR to measure: BASE's rate); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +13.1%/yr (no 2-yr run in FY18-FY18: BULL's rate); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: BHGE (retrospective, 2019-05-17) ◉ BUY — Ratio B -0.00x (-0.4% downside to Bear $23 / +87.7% upside to Bull $43) | Adj composite 2.75 vs market 1.47: gap +1.28 [UNDERVALUED] | +11% above the EPP floor $21 (46x FY19E $0.45) | Conservative 2-yr case: +64.0% total (+32.0%/yr) | At 50.9x FY19E the 15% hurdle price $30 sits at or below the BASE case; orders +8.7% and revenue +4.0% in Q1 2019, forward revenues +4% (no Q2 2019 revenue guide, Q1 2019 revenue as reported); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live from 2015-12-12 but scoped to oil, gas and coal reserves and refining; no theme in scope has dated evidence.
